clue.text: Herb as son, little fellow with endless merit

parts.note: a titch is a small person, British slang

indicators.note: endless says the word for merit loses its final letter

parts.note: worth means merit or value

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to describe someone called Herb as a son and a small man of little worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name but is the plant definition. TITCH is British slang for a small person; 'endless' cuts the last letter off WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitchwort is a small white-flowered wild plant, so it is a type of herb.

clue.text: The woman had something at the bottom of garden?

definitions.text: something at the bottom of garden?

parts.note: she stands for any woman
'd is the contracted form of had, as in she'd

explanation.surface: A woman owned something kept down at the end of her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The woman had' as the contraction she'd, and close it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is the small outbuilding traditionally found at the far end of a British garden.

clue.text: Number, say, being buried in Bury

indicators.note: being buried in says the example abbreviation sits inside the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
say, meaning for example, gives EG

explanation.surface: Bury, the Lancashire town, seems to have a number of something buried in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the English town, capitalised to hide that it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, so it is one kind of number.

clue.text: Keeping going in dialogue, getting two characters to switch around

indicators.text: getting two characters to switch around
indicators.note: two characters switching around says two letters of the word for dialogue trade places, here the V and the S

parts.note: a conversation is a dialogue

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a conversation going while a pair of people in a play swap roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the V and S of CONVERSATION gives the answer; 'in' just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation is the preserving of something, keeping it alive and in existence.

clue.text: Drilling completed? Congratulations!

definitions.meaning: a ..., read as two words, is a well that has been drilled to completion

explanation.surface: Someone is congratulated on finishing a drilling job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cheer of praise and, literally, a well whose drilling is finished.

clue.text: A number landing in gutter, dismissed

indicators.note: landing in says the article and number go inside the word for gutter

parts.note: a rut is a groove or channel, like a gutter

explanation.surface: A ball or a figure lands in the gutter and is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is run out when the stumps are broken before they reach the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Run out is one of the ways a cricket batsman can be dismissed.

clue.text: I left sailor travelling west for island

indicators.note: in an across clue, travelling west means the sailor's letters run right to left

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a sailor who heads westward towards an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue as I, L, AB; in the answer AB is turned round and comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island east of Java.

clue.text: They may go to bed after a journey

definitions.text: They may go to bed after a journey

parts.words: They may go to bed after a journey
parts.note: the bed is the sea bed, where heavy weights are dropped when a ship stops after a voyage

explanation.surface: Tired travellers head off to bed when they get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests sleep, but it is the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's iron weights are lowered to the sea bed to hold it in place at the end of a voyage.

clue.text: River suffering with lots of factories around?

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a trial is an ordeal or suffering

explanation.surface: A river suffers from all the factories built along its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial area is one dominated by factories and manufacturing.

clue.text: Getting snarled up — as net is here, before fishing

indicators.note: as the net is here refers back to the snarled-up state, so the three letters of net appear tangled

parts.note: angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fishing net gets tangled even before anyone starts fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is here' works because the clue's opening already says snarled up: the net is shown in that tangled state, so its three letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangling means getting caught up or twisted together.

clue.text: A group of coppers seen to be sharp

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A squad of police officers comes across as quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective means sharp or biting in taste or tone.

clue.text: Scientific study in which secondary aim is dicey

indicators.note: dicey suggests chance and risk, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a random order

explanation.surface: A research project where the subsidiary goal is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerodynamics is the branch of physics dealing with air flow around moving bodies.

clue.text: Some dog reared to be monster

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog raised by someone grows up to be a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'to be', which only links; the answer means monster, not 'to be monster'. 'reared' is part of the text, read forwards, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a kind of monster.

clue.text: Very small things not reused, chucked

indicators.note: chucked suggests things tossed about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Tiny items that weren't recycled have been thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuterons are atomic nuclei of heavy hydrogen, extremely small particles.

clue.text: Encouraged to be false with secret ultimately hidden

indicators.note: hidden says that letter is tucked inside the word for false

parts.note: simulated means fake or false

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of secret

explanation.surface: Someone was egged on to lie and keep a secret concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate someone is to rouse or spur them on.

clue.text: Blooming obsession that's absorbing Rex, four

indicators.note: that's absorbing says the obsession word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it
R is short for Rex, king
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An obsession that consumes King Rex and three others is going strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriving means flourishing, as healthy flowers do when in bloom.

clue.text: Tramp, maybe one emerging from papers

indicators.note: emerging from says the one comes out of the word for papers, leaving the rest

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vagrant might be someone crawling out from under a heap of newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture of a rough sleeper under newspapers is the misdirection; the papers are a file.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person or vagrant.

clue.text: After a day, person on slopes becomes more lively

indicators.note: after says the skier follows the day

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
a skier spends time on ski slopes

explanation.surface: After a day on the piste, a skier perks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and lively, so friskier is livelier.

clue.text: Greek character hugged by little child for a time

indicators.note: hugged by says the Greek letter sits inside the word for child

parts.note: a mite is a small child
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man gets a cuddle from a toddler for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a sixty-second unit, one particular span of clock time.

clue.text: Something that isn't a positive feature in puzzle?

parts.note: non- is the prefix of negation, something that is not
a plus is an advantage or good point

explanation.surface: A clue asking what counts as a drawback in a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or bewilder them, a verb sense of puzzle.

clue.text: Problematical situation that gets fellow reaching for hair dye?

definitions.meaning: a matter where right and wrong are unclear

definitions.text: gets fellow reaching for hair dye?
definitions.meaning: a patch of hair turning silver sends a man to the dye bottle

explanation.surface: A tricky matter is what drives a man to colour his hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an ill-defined, ambiguous matter, and literally a silvering patch of hair.

clue.text: Capital city's church featuring in adventure story

parts.note: Roman means belonging to Rome, the Italian capital
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church in a capital city plays a part in an adventure tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance in the old sense is a tale of chivalrous adventure.

clue.text: Project aiming at the stars? Something we laugh at

definitions.meaning: to send something up is to launch it skyward
a parody or spoof that mocks its target

explanation.surface: A space mission becomes a figure of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means launch upward; as a hyphenated noun it means a satirical imitation.

clue.text: Fellow surrounded by unsociable types who live in a city?

indicators.note: surrounded by says the fellow goes inside the unsociable types

parts.note: loners avoid company
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: An academic is hemmed in by recluses who all live in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners are the inhabitants of one particular city, London.

clue.text: Member meeting unknown host

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A club member meets a stranger who is the host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like someone entertaining guests; here it is a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, as in a heavenly host, especially of soldiers.

clue.text: Slight speech defect

explanation.surface: A minor impediment in someone's talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an insult and blurred articulation of words.

clue.text: Work that may be behind a counter

definitions.meaning: to work the soil by ploughing

definitions.text: that may be behind a counter
definitions.meaning: a cash register kept behind a shop counter

explanation.surface: A job working behind a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to cultivate land and also a shop's cash drawer.

clue.text: Extra lad, an idiot to be licked into shape

indicators.note: licking into shape means reforming something, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: One more boy, a fool who needs whipping into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional means extra, over and above what is already there.

clue.text: Money quietly given to party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Cash is handed over discreetly to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics but is a do, a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for money.

clue.text: Kit on the ground

parts.note: the ground is a sports ground, where players wear their kit

explanation.surface: Equipment lying on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ground' suggests lying on the floor; the ground is a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportswear is the clothing worn for games played at a sports ground.
